title: ESXi Inventory Drift from Approved Cluster Image
exclusions: Compares each latest collected ESXi `summary.config.product.version` and `summary.config.product.build` with an exact, effective-dated local desired-image record for its vCenter and cluster. A mismatch is inventory drift, not the native vSphere Lifecycle Manager compliance result: it does not compare vendor add-ons, firmware, drivers, components, hardware compatibility, desired-state validation, remediation eligibility, baseline compliance, advisories, reboot state, security severity, exploitability or successful patch installation. A matching build does not prove the complete image is compliant. Hosts without an authoritative desired-image row and stale/missing inventory are separate control-health failures and must not be treated as compliant. The rule never invokes a compliance check or remediation and makes no regulatory-attestation claim.
evidence: After deployment, retain governed host/cluster inventory; exported vSphere Lifecycle Manager desired-image identity and native compliance results; the approved `vsphere_desired_image.csv` revision with vCenter, cluster, version, build, image ID, approval and effective interval; add-on/DCN configuration; representative `VMInv:HostSystem` records and field/unit/time checks; source and lookup health; version-controlled `esxi_inventory_desired_image_drift` SPL, ACL, schedule, dispatch history and rows; dashboard/runbook revisions; owner dispositions and separately approved remediation records; and dated match, mismatch, no-policy, stale, duplicate, rename/move, delayed-data and rollback tests. This source review created no host inventory event, vLCM compliance run, patch, reboot, remediation, Splunk execution or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In isolated inventory fixtures, supply host `esx01.example`, vCenter `vc01.example`, cluster `prod-a`, version `8.0.3`, build `24859861`, a distinct inventory time, and a lookup row effective at that time specifying desired version `8.0.3` and build `24674464`. Expect exactly one `inventory_build_mismatch` row preserving actual and desired values, image ID, lookup approval and UC-2.1.14.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero drift rows when actual version/build exactly match one active desired row. Do not classify as compliant when the lookup is absent/expired/duplicated, host/vCenter/cluster/version/build is blank, inventory is older than the accepted freshness limit, source/index is wrong, or the event is outside the range; separate health searches must surface each case and disagreement with native vLCM compliance.

dataSources: Primary source is vCenter HostSystem inventory collected through Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics with `hostinv` into the deployment-selected inventory index (documented default `index=vmware-inv`), `source=VMInv:HostSystem`, and `sourcetype=vmware_inframon:inv:hostsystem`. Required documented fields are host name (`name` or `summary.config.name`), `summary.config.product.version`, `summary.config.product.build`, vCenter, cluster identity/topology, and collection/index time. The governed local lookup `vsphere_desired_image.csv` is populated from approved vSphere Lifecycle Manager image state and includes exact version/build, image ID, approval, effective dates and owner. Native vLCM compliance/export is the authoritative comparison point.
app: Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (Splunkbase 5089) collects vCenter host inventory through Data Collection Nodes. A local platform-governance app owns desired-image ingestion, temporal lookup, inventory/compliance health, saved search, tests, dashboard, routing and runbook.
spl:
index=vmware-inv source="VMInv:HostSystem" sourcetype="vmware_inframon:inv:hostsystem" earliest=-2h@h latest=-1h@h
| eval esxi_host=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(name),""),nullif(trim('summary.config.name'),""))), vcenter=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(vcenter),""),nullif(trim(host),""))), cluster_name=coalesce(nullif(trim(cluster_name),""),nullif(trim(cluster),"")), actual_version=trim('summary.config.product.version'), actual_build=trim('summary.config.product.build')
| where len(esxi_host)>0 AND len(vcenter)>0 AND len(cluster_name)>0 AND len(actual_version)>0 AND len(actual_build)>0
| stats latest(_time) AS inventory_time latest(_indextime) AS inventory_index_time latest(actual_version) AS actual_version latest(actual_build) AS actual_build BY vcenter cluster_name esxi_host
| lookup vsphere_desired_image.csv vcenter cluster_name OUTPUT desired_version desired_build desired_image_id approved_by valid_from valid_until
| where len(desired_version)>0 AND len(desired_build)>0 AND inventory_time>=strptime(valid_from,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") AND inventory_time<strptime(valid_until,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") AND (actual_version!=desired_version OR actual_build!=desired_build)
| eval drift_reason="inventory_build_mismatch", use_case="UC-2.1.14"
| table inventory_time vcenter cluster_name esxi_host actual_version actual_build desired_version desired_build desired_image_id approved_by valid_from valid_until drift_reason inventory_index_time use_case
| sort 0 vcenter cluster_name esxi_host
description: Reports the latest complete ESXi host-inventory row when its exact product version or build differs from the effective approved cluster-image record. Each result is one host-level inventory mismatch requiring reconciliation with native Lifecycle Manager compliance.
value: A controlled version/build comparison quickly exposes hosts upgraded outside the approved cluster image, lagging a desired build, or attached to the wrong policy. Keeping native image-compliance evidence separate prevents a simple inventory match from being overstated as firmware, driver or security-patch assurance.
implementation: Collect HostSystem inventory and export approved vLCM desired-image state into a versioned, effective-dated lookup. Run the closed hourly search, validate exact fields and one policy row per cluster, route mismatches to lifecycle owners, and reconcile every row with the native vSphere Client image/compliance view before any remediation.
visualization: Use a host table showing inventory time, vCenter, cluster, host, actual and desired version/build, image ID, lookup validity, native vLCM status, owner, maintenance and disposition. Add mismatch counts by cluster/build and separate panels for stale inventory, missing/duplicate/expired desired rows, and native-compliance disagreement. Never label matching inventory as fully patched.
schema: vCenter HostSystem inventory plus governed effective-dated vLCM desired-image lookup
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM dataset documents ESXi product version/build or vLCM desired-image identity. Keep raw inventory and authoritative lookup/native-compliance reconciliation as the primary contract.

knownFalsePositives:
A mismatch can be expected but still requires explicit evidence.

1. **Approved staged rollout** — canary hosts may intentionally lead or lag the cluster image. Match host, target build, phase, owner and finite interval.

2. **Emergency out-of-band patch** — an urgent ISO/offline-bundle upgrade can place a host ahead of desired state. Confirm the approved exception and update the authoritative image rather than suppressing indefinitely.

3. **Host moved between clusters** — inventory and policy exports can be temporally inconsistent. Reconcile move time, current parent and policy effective interval.

4. **vCenter/add-on inventory lag** — incremental collection, DCN backlog or failed hostinv task can preserve old version/build. Compare current Host Summary and collection health.

5. **Desired lookup lag or duplicate** — an image update not yet exported, overlapping rows or case mismatch can create false drift. Fail lookup health closed; do not select an arbitrary row.

6. **Build-string formatting drift** — whitespace or type conversion can differ even when values look similar. Preserve raw fields and normalize only documented formatting.

7. **Native vLCM richer result** — host can match ESXi build but differ in add-on, component, firmware or driver state, or can mismatch while native compliance explains an incompatible image. Native status governs remediation.

8. **Standalone/baseline-managed host** — a cluster-image lookup may not apply. Inventory management mode and policy scope before inclusion.

**Suppression mechanism:** use a governed post-result exception keyed by vCenter plus stable host identity and exact actual/desired build pair, with lifecycle mode, reason, ticket, owner and finite expiry. Never suppress an entire cluster or treat a missing desired row as compliant.
mitreAttack: N/A (ESXi lifecycle inventory governance; no adversary behavior asserted)
detectionType: Exact host inventory versus approved image mismatch
hardware: ESXi hosts managed by vCenter. vLCM image applicability depends on vSphere release, cluster/standalone lifecycle mode, hardware compatibility, vendor add-on, firmware and drivers.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and authority

Assign vSphere lifecycle, hardware, security, Splunk and change owners. Inventory every vCenter, cluster and standalone host with lifecycle mode, desired-image owner, maintenance policy and stable host identity. Broadcom describes vLCM Images as declarative desired state including ESXi version, vendor add-on, firmware and drivers. This UC intentionally compares only product version/build inventory; native vLCM compliance remains authoritative for the complete image.

## Step 1 — Collect HostSystem inventory

Deploy supported Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics and configure vCenter API access over TCP 443. Include `hostinv` in the collection pool. Verify the documented default `index=vmware-inv`, `source=VMInv:HostSystem`, and `sourcetype=vmware_inframon:inv:hostsystem`, or replace only the local index in the SPL. Compare sampled records with vSphere Client Host > Summary. Prove `summary.config.product.version`, `summary.config.product.build`, host name, vCenter, cluster mapping, `_time` and `_indextime`.

Create inventory health for expected hosts, last successful hostinv job, records_written, stale and future times, missing product fields, duplicate host identities, cluster-parent drift, vCenter auth/API errors and DCN backlog. A missing host is not compliant.

## Step 2 — Govern desired-image data

Export the approved cluster image from vSphere Lifecycle Manager through an owner-approved API or controlled process. Build `vsphere_desired_image.csv` with lowercase vCenter, exact cluster name, desired version/build, immutable image or policy ID, approved_by, source revision, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, owner and extraction time. Require one active row per in-scope cluster and reject overlaps, gaps, malformed UTC timestamps and unapproved edits. Record whether each scope is image-managed, baseline-managed or unsupported.

Separately retain native vLCM compliance and last check time. Do not synthesize full compliance from the lookup. A host whose build matches can still have component, add-on, firmware or driver drift.

## Step 3 — Schedule and validate the search

Save the sidecar SPL as `esxi_inventory_desired_image_drift` and run hourly after measured inventory delay. Its closed range is one hour, delayed by one hour. `stats latest` selects the newest complete inventory per vCenter/cluster/host. The temporal lookup must be active at that inventory time. Exact inequality on version or build yields one `inventory_build_mismatch` row.

Test exact match; version-only and build-only mismatch; host ahead and behind; no, expired and overlapping lookup; host rename/move; blank fields; stale inventory; duplicate events; late/future data; vCenter case; and same host name in two vCenters. Compare results with vSphere Client > Cluster > Updates > Image > Compliance using a freshly run native check. Assert that Splunk never labels a match fully compliant.

## Step 4 — Respond safely

Dashboard the mismatch plus current native compliance, desired-image revision, maintenance, host connection/maintenance state and owner. Triage by verifying raw inventory and collection health, validating lookup scope/effective time, checking current Host Summary, then reviewing native image compliance and compatibility. Classify approved rollout, emergency exception, stale collection, lookup defect, lifecycle-mode mismatch or unexplained drift.

Never trigger check compliance, remediation, maintenance mode, evacuation or reboot automatically. Lifecycle remediation can affect workload availability and hardware support. Use the approved vSphere change workflow with DRS/HA capacity, backups, hardware compatibility, rollback and service validation.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- No host rows: verify `hostinv`, API credentials/443, source/index/sourcetype, DCN workers, forwarding and Splunk RBAC.
- Product fields null: inspect raw inventory, add-on Inventory Reference and host/vCenter version; do not extract build from `fullName` unless separately tested.
- Policy miss: verify exact vCenter/cluster normalization, lifecycle mode, export freshness and effective UTC range.
- Mismatch after remediation: wait for fresh inventory, confirm host reboot and actual build, rerun native compliance, and inspect collection delay.
- Match but native noncompliant: expected for richer image components; route native result and do not weaken it.
- Native compliant but Splunk mismatch: align collection time, cluster/image revision, build formatting and host move history.

Keep status draft until lifecycle and Splunk owners validate the policy pipeline, native comparison, fixtures and response. Documentation review is not patch assurance.
grandmaExplanation: We compare each virtualization host's recorded software version with the exact version its cluster owner approved. A difference starts a review, but the official lifecycle tool still decides whether the whole host image, including drivers and firmware, is compliant.
